critical.finding: Book growth is pinned at the engine's generic BOOK_GROWTH_CAP of 8%/yr, and the payout rationale calls this 'its own five-year common-equity growth 8.0%'. That is false: Nu's own common equity grew 4,441m (2021) -> 11,291m (2025), about 26%/yr; 6,406m (2023) -> 11,291m (2025), about 33%/yr; and +17% in H1 2026 alone (to 13,250m), mostly retained earnings plus BRL translation, not issuance. The cap (forecast_financials.py BOOK_GROWTH_CAP) is a rule, not company data. Through payout = max(0.5, 1 - g/ROE) it forces base payouts of 73-77% (bull similar) for ten years, so base EPS grows only about 6-7%/yr (0.684 -> 0.830 by 2030) against reported NI growth of +46% in FY2025 and +62% y/y in H1 2026 (about +36% tax-normalized). Retained profit at a 26-29% ROE against an 11.2% cost of equity is the main value driver of a bank in residual income, so this rule largely sets the result. The binding company constraint is regulatory capital, not an 8% cap (see the CET1 finding).

critical.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, written from 2029-11): NU failed because the 2025-26 ROE of ~30% was a peak built on three things that all reversed together. (1) Credit: management deliberately moved into 'higher-risk, higher-return segments' (dc_rel_q2_2026), secured lending growth stalled (~+3% QoQ in Q2'26 vs +133% y/y in Q3'25), Stage 2 rose 10.1% -> 11.9% of gross and NPL 90+ hit 6.9% (7-quarter high) while Brazil household defaults hit a record 8.09% (mc_rt_default); IFRS 9 front-loading on a 44%-growing book hid the true loss rate until growth slowed, then cost of risk jumped and ROE fell to the 2023 level (~17%) or below. (2) Capital: CET1 fell 13.0% -> 11.9% in six months (RWA +14.7% vs CET1 +5.4%, dc_fs_q2_2026) while US$1bn was spent on buybacks; capital forced a slowdown in loan growth exactly when growth was the thesis. (3) Brazil macro/policy: Lula's re-election (2026-10-25) weakened BRL ~10% intraday, 91% of revenue is Brazilian, CSLL rises to 20% from 2028 and BCB limits unsolicited credit marketing from 2027; meanwhile the 14.2% Q2'26 tax rate (671m deferred-tax benefit) normalized, cutting reported EPS ~15%. Add management turnover (CFO replaced July 2026, CTO resigned effective 2026-11-12) and a new US cost centre with no revenue. Early signals: Q3'26 (2026-11-12) NPL 90+ >= 7.0% and NPL 15-90 not falling seasonally; Stage 2 share > 12%; CET1 < 11.5% or buyback paused; IFRS effective tax back >= 25%; ECL growth > portfolio growth for a second quarter; BRL/USD not recovering by the 2026-12-08 Investor Day; risk-adjusted NIM back below 10%.

critical.finding: The base case contradicts its own story. Core/field/path base say the credit book keeps growing fast (+44% y/y, dc_k_portfolio) at a normalized ROE of 26-28%, but the residual-income engine assumes payout 73-77% every year (assumption 'payout': 'no distribution history: 50% assumed ... book growth bounded 3.0%-8.0%'), i.e. book equity growth capped at 8%. Actual parent equity grew 11.29bn -> 13.25bn in H1'26 alone (~+17% in six months) and Nu pays no dividend. Result: base EPS path FY2027 0.684, +6-7% a year thereafter (company_path.scenarios.base.economics.fiscal_years), BELOW the FY2026 run-rate (H1'26 diluted EPS 0.3936; FY2025 0.5846). A base in which EPS falls from 2026 to 2027 while the book grows 40% is not the most likely path; the base value 7.14 (-39% vs 11.65) rests on this cap. The same 75% payout is also incompatible with the CET1 constraint argued in the bear (a bank growing RWA ~30%/yr must retain, not distribute).
critical.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json val.case.scenarios[base].periods[].payout_fraction and assumptions id=payout; company_path.scenarios.base.economics.fiscal_years; position/core.json thesis_he.base
